kana.title: Kana and sound
kana.body: Kana represent sound units, not English letters. Learn each script separately. Romanisation in clues is a reading aid; type the Japanese answer. Basic kana omit voiced and contracted combinations, which come later.

Japanese phonology: morae, consonants and vowels

mora.title: Morae and length
mora.body: Long vowels and a small っ change meaning. おばさん has four morae; おばあさん has five. A small っ occupies a mora and lengthens the following consonant. IPA here gives broad standard-Tokyo segments, not pitch accent; vowel devoicing and detailed allophones are not encoded.

loanwords.title: Katakana words
loanwords.body: Katakana is commonly used for loanwords. The mark ー lengthens the preceding vowel. Spell these words in katakana, including small characters and the length mark.

greetings.title: Greetings and politeness
greetings.body: Choose expressions for the situation. おはようございます is a polite morning greeting; おはよう is casual. Set phrases are learned as phrases. The は in こんにちは and こんばんは is pronounced /wa/.

Japanese grammar: particles and polite forms

clarification.title: Asking for help
clarification.body: Use short polite phrases to ask for repetition, slower speech or a word’s meaning. もう一度 means once more. These boards practise language, not listening comprehension.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio
Japanese grammar: particles and polite forms

copula.title: Topics and polite noun sentences
copula.body: X は Y です introduces X as the topic and says it is Y. The particle は is written ha but pronounced /wa/. か marks a question. ではありません is a polite negative; じゃありません is also accepted here. Japanese does not mark grammatical gender or add a/an.

Japanese grammar: particles and polite forms

residence.title: Origin and residence
residence.body: から can mark origin. に marks the place of residence with 住んでいます. Use polite forms here; an origin phrase and a residence phrase make different claims.

sources.title: Japan Foundation: Irodori Starter (A1), study and audio
Japanese grammar: particles and polite forms

numbers.title: Numbers and age
numbers.body: Numbers have several readings. This board accepts し for four, しち for seven and く for nine alongside よん, なな and きゅう. Age uses the counter 歳, with changes such as いっさい and はっさい, and the special form はたち for twenty. It is not a complete system of counters.
